status: Specified locally before new frozen-branch measurement; not a public preregistration. Prior online outcomes are already known.
question: How much do updates after the strategy switch contribute, compared with freezing the identical policy at that boundary?

uncertainty.scope: Paired percentile bootstrap over twelve independent replicate seeds. Each seed controls policy, map perturbations and player parameters using separate streams; cases and rounds are averaged within seed. Intervals describe this generator and four fixed family combinations, not humans or arbitrary games.

primary: Online minus boundary-frozen enemy damage in switch rounds 9–12, equal-weighting the four known cases within each of 12 seeds.

criterion.interpretation: A useful local post-switch effect requires mean >=3 HP and 95% lower bound >0. This diagnostic does not select or promote a new learner.

procedure: Restore each archived pretraining snapshot, replay all 12 repeat encounters exactly, save checkpoint, and fork online/frozen. Replay the 12 online switch encounters exactly against the archive; count these as reused evidence. Score 12 new frozen encounters. Independently verify choice/feedback/commit traces and replay every combat.
limits: Known cases and known online outcomes; prospective frozen control, not fresh held-out validation.
Intervals resample seeds, not rounds or authored family identities.
Difference estimates the contribution of allowing updates after this boundary, including effects on later sampled tactics and physical encounters.
Enemy damage is a capability measure, not fun or fairness.
Primary diverse arm; narrow/per-case comparisons exploratory and unadjusted.

demonstration.selection: Chosen before new frozen outcomes; retain even if inconclusive.
